senses.gloss: חִסֵּד, חִשֵּׂד [to scrape off,] (cmp. גדף, גרף) to jeer, scoff at, to shame.
units: <cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 7:12">Ruth R. to IV, 8</cite> <he>שחִסְּדָן ברבים</he> (or <he>שחֲסָדָן</he>; ed. Wil. <he>שחשדן</he>) he scoffed at them publicly (speaking ironically, with ref. to <cite ref="II Chronicles 13:8">II Chr. XIII, 8</cite>); Y. Yeb. XVII, beg. 15ᶜ <he>שחִישֵּׂד וכ׳</he> he jeered at Jeroboam; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 65">Gen. R. s. 65</cite>; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 65">ib.</cite> s. 73 <he>שחסדם</he> ed. Wil. (oth. <he>שחש׳</he>); <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 33">Lev. R. s. 33</cite>; Midr. Sam. ch. XVIII <he>שחִיסְּדָן</he>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 205">Yalk. Kings 205</cite> <he>ומְחַשֵּׂד</he>.—
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 30:16">Ex. R. s. 30</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 2:14">Ex. II, 14</cite>) <he>שחִיסְּדוּ וכ׳</he> when Dathan and Abiram sneered at him.

<cite ref="Exodus 2:14">Ib.</cite> <he>בזה שחִיסַּדְתֶּם אותו וכ׳</he> with the very word (<cite ref="U00495"><he>שופט</he></cite>) with which you sneered at him, I shall give him the rulership <he>(משפטים</he>).
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 42:1">Pesik. R. s. 42</cite> <he>מְחַסְּדִים את שרה</he> (not <he>מחסרו׳</he>) jeered at Sarah; a. e.—V. <cite ref="H00829"><he>חִיסּוּד</he></cite>.
